subject: Physics
_transcription: Physics = pages p08-p09 (printed page numbers 10-11) under the 'Physics' heading: Q46-Q53 on p08, Q54-Q60 on p09. The paper numbers its 60 questions straight through, so Physics' printed numbers 46-60 are restarted as ref/questionNumber 1-15 (printed 46 = ref 1 ... printed 60 = ref 15). Numbers checked unbroken 46..60 against the printed 'N.' labels. No answer key. Stem figures sit to the right of the question text: refs 1 (PV cycle), 3 (ln R vs t plot), 7 (circuit), 9 (diode circuit), 11 (magnets and copper loop), 13 (RC circuit), 15 (capacitor trajectories). Options keep their printed trailing full stops; dense options were read from 260 dpi renders.

rows.text: A Copper wire of length \(L_{\mathrm{Cu}}\), Young's modulus \(Y_{\mathrm{Cu}}\), and diameter \(d\) is hung from the ceiling. An Aluminium wire of length \(L_{\mathrm{Al}}\), Young's modulus \(Y_{\mathrm{Al}}\), and of same diameter \(d\) is joined end-to-end at the free end of the Copper wire. If under the action of a load applied at the free end of the Aluminium wire the net elongation is \(\Delta L\), the applied load is
options: \(\frac{\pi d^2 \Delta L (Y_{\mathrm{Cu}} L_{\mathrm{Al}} - Y_{\mathrm{Al}} L_{\mathrm{Cu}})}{4 L_{\mathrm{Cu}} L_{\mathrm{Al}}}\).
\(\frac{\pi d^2 \Delta L (Y_{\mathrm{Cu}} L_{\mathrm{Al}} + Y_{\mathrm{Al}} L_{\mathrm{Cu}})}{4 L_{\mathrm{Cu}} L_{\mathrm{Al}}}\).
\(\frac{\pi d^2 Y_{\mathrm{Cu}} Y_{\mathrm{Al}} \Delta L}{4 (Y_{\mathrm{Cu}} L_{\mathrm{Al}} + Y_{\mathrm{Al}} L_{\mathrm{Cu}})}\).

rows.subtopic: Gravitational Potential Energy and Escape Speed
rows.text: What should be the closest approximate radius of a celestial body twice as massive as the sun so that the escape speed from the celestial body is equal to the speed of light? (The mass of sun is \(2 \times 10^{30}\) Kg, speed of light is \(3 \times 10^8\) m/s, and universal gravitational constant \(G = 7 \times 10^{-11}\) N m\(^2\)/Kg\(^2\).)

rows.subtopic: Displacement Relation in a Progressive Wave
rows.text: The transverse displacement at position \(x\) and time \(t\) in a string due to a travelling wave is given by \(y(x, t) = 3.0\cos(\pi x - 4\pi t)\) cm, where \(x\) is in centimeters and \(t\) is in seconds. Which of the following statements is wrong?
options: Maximum value of transverse velocity of any point is \(12\pi\) cm/s and wavelength is 0.2 m.
Speed of wave propagation in the +ve \(x\)-direction is \(4\pi\) cm/s.
Transverse velocity at \(t = 0\) and \(x = 0.25\) cm is \(6\sqrt{2}\pi\) cm/s.
Maximum value of transverse acceleration of any point is \(48\pi^2\) cm/s\(^2\).

rows.text: An electron of mass \(m_e\) and charge \(e\) is projected with a speed \(v\) making an angle \(\theta\) with respect to the top electrode of a parallel plate capacitor as shown in the figure. Considering only the effect of the downward constant electric field \(E\) on the electron's motion, which of the following statements is correct.
options: Electron moves along trajectory C with a time of flight given by \((m_e v/eE)\sin^2\theta\).
Electron moves along trajectory C with a maximum horizontal displacement given by \((m_e v^2 \sin 2\theta)/eE\).
Electron moves along trajectory A with a horizontal displacement given by \(v\cos\theta\sqrt{2dm_e/eE}\).
Electron moves along trajectory B with a final velocity \(v\cos\theta\) parallel to the electrodes.

figure.note: Two horizontal plates a distance d apart; field E shown by a downward arrow. The electron starts at the top plate with velocity v directed down and to the right at angle theta below the top plate. Three dashed paths: A, a straight line down to the bottom plate; B, curving and levelling off parallel to the plates; C, curving back up to the top plate.
